extracted.intended_audience: graduate students (Math 216) studying algebraic geometry; readers of Ravi Vakil's 'The Rising Sea'
extracted.subtask_description: Reading and using textbook lecture-notes on advanced algebraic geometry topics (Stein factorization, Zariski's Main Theorem, Castelnuovo criterion, Formal Functions, Serre duality) aimed at graduate students following Math 216.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stein factorization construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a proper morphism π : X → Y of locally Noetherian schemes, define Y' := Spec π_* O_X; then π factors as X --α--> Y' --β--> Y with β finite and α O-connected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By Grothendieck's Coherence Theorem π_* O_X is coherent (of finite type), so Y' is well-defined and β is finite. To check O-connectedness of α, use quasicoherence and check on an affine cover pulled back from Y; on affines the relevant maps of sections are explicit isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: O-connectedness criterion for birational proper morphisms (Exercise 29.5.B)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is a proper morphism of locally Noetherian schemes that is an isomorphism over a dense open subset of Y and Y is normal, then π is O-connected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies, for example, to blow-ups of smooth varieties along smooth centers. Use Zariski's Connectedness Lemma and properties of normalization/Stein factorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of contractions determined by locus contracted (Exercise 29.5.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y and π' : X → Y' are proper morphisms of locally Noetherian schemes each contracting the same connected set of X (and are isomorphisms elsewhere), and Y and Y' are normal, then π and π' are the same up to unique isomorphism of targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify Y and Y' as topological spaces, recover structure sheaf via Stein factorization (π_* O_X) to get the scheme structure; hence the target is determined by the contracted locus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stein factorization commutes with flat base change (Exercise 29.5.D)
rubrics_metrics.description: The construction of the Stein factorization of a morphism of locally Noetherian schemes commutes with any flat base change Z → Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use functoriality of pushforward and formation of Spec of π_* O_X under flat base change; check coherence/specialization on affines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution of singularities for (reduced projective) curves via normalization and blowing up
rubrics_metrics.description: For a reduced projective curve C over a field k, normalization ν : C~ → C resolves singularities; alternatively, an algorithm of repeatedly blowing up singular points terminates because blowing up decreases the arithmetic genus pa, and pa(C~) is a lower bound throughout the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key subclaims: (i) if pa(C) = pa(C~) then ν is an isomorphism (C is already nonsingular); (ii) for finite morphism C' → C we have pa(C') ≤ pa(C); (iii) blowing up a singular point decreases pa. Use exact sequence 0 → O_C → π_* O_{C'} → G → 0 where G is supported on finite points, so χ computations give pa inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: O-connectedness implies isomorphism for curves (Exercise 29.5.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : C' → C (finite morphism between reduced curves, isomorphism off finite set) is O-connected then π is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Zariski's Connectedness Lemma to deduce connected fibers and bijectivity; identify C and C' as topological spaces and use the isomorphism O_C → π_* O_{C'} to identify the ringed space structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zariski's Main Theorem (Grothendieck's form, 29.6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a proper morphism π : X → Y of locally Noetherian schemes: (a) the set X0 of points of X isolated in their fiber is open; (b) the restriction π|_{X0} factors as an open embedding followed by a finite morphism (X0 → Y' → Y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof strategy: take Stein factorization X --α--> Y' --β--> Y and reduce to the O-connected case; identify X0 with the unramified locus (where Ω_α = 0), which is open; show α|_{X0} is an open embedding and gives the desired factorization. For varieties the argument simplifies via upper semicontinuity of fiber dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of finite morphisms (29.6.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For π : X → Y a morphism of locally Noetherian schemes, the following are equivalent: (a) π is finite; (b) π is affine and proper; (c) π is proper and quasi-finite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finite ⇒ affine + proper by definition and basic results. Affine + proper ⇒ finite fibers (exercise), hence proper + finite fibers gives quasi-finite. For (c) ⇒ (a) apply Zariski's Main Theorem to get factorization as quasicompact open embedding into a finite morphism; cancellation theorems then yield finiteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local compactification hypothesis (†) and Nagata compactification context
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism π : X → Y of locally Noetherian schemes satisfies (†) if for some affine cover {U_i} of Y, each restriction π|_{π^{-1}(U_i)} factors as an open embedding into a scheme proper over U_i. A morphism satisfying (†) is necessarily separated and finite type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nagata's compactification theorem implies that every separated finite type morphism of Noetherian schemes satisfies (†) (more generally for quasicompact quasiseparated targets). Use this hypothesis in exercises about open embeddings and quasi-finite morphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasi-finite birational morphisms to normal targets are open embeddings under (†) (Exercise 29.6.D)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is a quasi-finite birational morphism of integral locally Noetherian schemes, Y normal, and π satisfies (†), then π is an open embedding (and if bijective then an isomorphism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Zariski's Main Theorem locally and use normality to extend local identifications globally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasi-finite morphisms factor as open embedding into finite morphism (Exercise 29.6.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is a quasi-finite morphism of Noetherian schemes (satisfying the appropriate hypotheses), then π factors as an open embedding into a finite morphism X → Y' → Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interprets quasi-finite morphisms as 'open subsets of finite morphisms'—this is an application of Zariski's Main Theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Castelnuovo's Criterion for contracting (-1)-curves (29.7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a smooth projective surface over k and C ⊂ X is a (-1)-curve (isomorphic to P^1 with normal bundle O(-1), self-intersection -1), then there exists a birational morphism π : X → Y contracting C to a k-valued point q; Y is a smooth projective surface, π is the blow-up of Y at q, and C is the exceptional divisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof in three steps: (1) construct a base-point-free invertible sheaf L (from a very ample H with H^1(X,H)=0 and twisting by multiples of C) whose complete linear series yields a morphism contracting C; (2) normalize image and use Theorem on Formal Functions to prove smoothness of Y at the contraction point; (3) use universal property of blow-up and cancellation theorems to identify π as the blow-up at q. Exercises guide the technical details (vanishing, degree computations, formal functions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to construct contraction via line bundle (Step 1 of Castelnuovo proof)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose a very ample H with H^1(X,H)=0, take k large, set L := H(kC); show H^1(X, H(iC)) = 0 for 0 ≤ i ≤ k, show L is base-point-free, and that the map given by |L| contracts C (deg L|_C = 0) while embedding X  ackslash C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the map H^0(X,H) → H^0(X,H(kC)) and surjectivity onto H^0(C, L|_C) to handle base points on C; use vanishing for away-from-C base points. Then take image in projective space and normalize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem on Formal Functions (29.8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let X → Spec B be a proper morphism with B Noetherian and F a coherent sheaf on X. For an ideal I ⊂ B, let ^B = lim B/I^{n+1} and X_n = X ×_{Spec B} Spec(B/I^{n+1}), F_n the pullback of F. Then for all i the natural map Hi(X,F) ⊗_B ^B → lim Hi(X_n, F_n) is an isomorphism of topological ^B-modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses: Grothendieck's Coherence Theorem (Hi(X,F) finitely generated B-module), rewrite Hi(X_n,F_n) as Hi(X, F / I^{n}F), use long exact sequences and limits, employ Rees algebra R• and graded-module finiteness to get Artin–Rees-type statements that show cofinality of images im(u_n) with I-adic topology and eventual annihilation properties; conclude isomorphism of completed modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Rees algebra and graded module finiteness in formal functions proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Form the Rees algebra R• = ⊕_{m≥0} I^m; the graded modules ⊕_{n≥0} H^i(X, I^n F) are finitely generated R•-modules, hence satisfy eventual relation I·im(u_n) = im(u_{n+1}) beyond some n_0 (Artin–Rees style).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This yields control of images im(u_n) and of kernels ker(v_n), allowing identification of limit terms and proving the Theorem on Formal Functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desideratum: canonical dualizing sheaf ω_X for smooth varieties (30.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For smooth X one desires ω_X = det Ω_X (the determinant of the cotangent bundle) to be a dualizing sheaf; in that case ω_X is an invertible sheaf (the canonical bundle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishing this requires additional work (later exercises—e.g., 30.4.I) and is harder than basic duality statements; it holds at least when X is a regular embedding into a smooth variety (exercise 30.4.H).

rubrics_metrics.name: Desideratum: Serre duality for vector bundles (functorial and trace versions, 30.1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is projective of pure dimension n and F is locally free, the desired functorial statement is Hi(X,F) ≅ H^{n-i}(X, F^∨ ⊗ ω_X)^∨ (equivalently a perfect pairing functorial in F). The trace version is constructed from cup product Hi(X,F) × H^{n-i}(X, F^∨ ⊗ ω_X) → H^n(X, ω_X) and a trace map t : H^n(X, ω_X) → k producing a perfect pairing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The trace version (via cup product + trace) yields the functorial version. For Cohen–Macaulay X (in particular smooth X) the trace version holds; the text will prove the functorial version (Corollary 30.3.9) and indicate how to get the trace version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desideratum: Serre duality for Hom (functorial and trace versions, 30.1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any coherent sheaf F on a pure n-dimensional projective k-scheme X, one expects a functorial isomorphism Hom(F, ω_X) ≅ H^n(X, F)^∨. The trace version uses the natural pairing Hom(F, ω_X) × H^n(X, F) → H^n(X, ω_X) and a linear functional t on H^n(X, ω_X) giving a perfect pairing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The covariance of H^n(X,-) gives the candidate pairing; here the functorial version implies the trace version. The text outlines these versions and indicates which hypotheses (e.g., Cohen–Macaulay) guarantee which versions.
